replies.body: Close Call showed 'NVDA above $150' odds taken from the $149/$152.5 spread, which is really the chance of a close above $150.75 (1-2 pts off). The odds are now read at $150 itself from the strikes either side, and the note under them says which prices were used.

Close Call showed AAPL at 50% odds to close above $360 while YES cost $204 for a $500 payout (41%): a finance professor would call that a free-money bug. Each strike is now priced at its own implied volatility, so YES costs the market's own spread price and agrees with the odds.

A user who saw '+9 pts' on a call had no way to tell skill from luck. My beliefs now marks each graded call on the spread of calls like it (e.g. 'in the best 1 in 10; about 1 in 10 calls do this well, so one call still says little about skill').

The brain learns each news headline and its opposite. 4 in 10 opposites were bet the same way as the headline (e.g. 'I don't think the retail recovery will stall' -> Target down). Now a stock can't be bet the same way on both sides, and users who type 'I don't think...' get the opposite bet.
On a phone the strategist family tree showed only the first 5 of 11 generations, so the current leaders were off screen. It now fits the whole tree in the card, newest on the right.
A 42% hit rate reads like a coin flip with small stakes. The base-rate line now also shows the range: about 12 pts either way vs the S&P for a single 90-day call, from the app's own graded calls.

A professor would ask 'compared to what?' about the strategists' +2.6 pts. The board now shows the app's own pick (+2.6) and a random idea (+0.3) on the same calls, so nobody mistakes a tie for a win.
A finance professor would ask how 114k picks got graded in two weeks. The Brain page now says it plainly: 5,474 real-time grades, the rest practice calls graded from history.

Close Call now shows each user their own record against the market's odds: 'You were right 7 of 14; the market's odds expected 6.7', with an honest skill-or-luck line. Each answer also shows the odds the market gave it.
